headline: CISA says Node2Shell is now exploited as the PHP2Shell deadline hits tomorrow; Sony's So-net breach exposes 2.6 million records

bullets.text: New: CISA warns that hackers are now exploiting the critical Node2Shell flaw. Treat it as active exploitation and follow vendor guidance for fixed releases.

PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) is exploited in the wild and remains the top story at 8 outlets. CISA's federal due date is tomorrow, 2026-10-29. Fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35.

PolyShell attacks on Adobe Commerce have breached hundreds of stores, and exploit traffic for the Brotli 'HTTP2Shell' flaw has emerged. CVE-2026-48356 (Magento) and CVE-2026-111497 (Brotli) are in CISA KEV, due 2026-11-10; Microsoft shipped emergency .NET patches.
New: a breach at Sony-owned internet provider So-net compromised 2.6 million customer records. The University of Copenhagen breach exposed data of 525,000 people.

Japan's GMO is offering a $1 million bounty over its FX trading cloud breach. Ransomware is still disrupting care at UNM Health and hit Bajaj Hospital in India. The ShinyHunters-exploited PeopleSoft zero-day (CVE-2026-35273) is three chained flaws.

Supply chain: the LiteLLM 1.107.0 compromise on PyPI and Docker began with an exposed master key. A worm armed 42 GitHub repos and 'Gheist' uses stolen GitHub tokens to steal cloud secrets. Last 7 days at 1.02x the 90-day average.

actions: Find any Node2Shell-affected systems you run, apply the vendor's fix now and check exposed hosts for compromise.
Update PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 before CISA's 2026-10-29 due date, rebuild images that bundle PHP, and check exposed PHP hosts.
Patch Adobe Commerce and Magento for CVE-2026-48356 and check stores for webshells and unexpected uploaded files.
Apply Microsoft's emergency .NET patches for Brotli CVE-2026-111497 and track fixes from other software that bundles Brotli.
Apply Oracle's fixes for the PeopleSoft chain (CVE-2026-35273) and review PeopleSoft access logs for signs of data theft.
Search lockfiles, images and CI caches for litellm 1.107.0; if it ran, treat the host as compromised and rotate every credential it could read.
